articles.title: Socialism Deferred: The Communist Party of Italy and the Historic Compromise of 1976
articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: American politics is at a crossroads. All that was once considered certain or possible is now in question. For the first time since the early 20th century, American Socialists are gaining considerable municipal and state level influence through successful and highly publicized electoral campaigns. After a largely successful midterm showing, the DSA established itself as a small but potent force in American politics. For the first time there is a comparatively large cohort of elected DSA members holding local, state, and federal office. Along with this heightened political influence comes greater political risk. articles.title: Fujimori government revives war on the left with detentions of artists and activists
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Organizations in Peru raised the alarm about the arbitrary arrest of several progressive artists and activists on November 19. The arrests were reportedly carried out by the Counterterrorism Directorate (DIRCOTE) in the cities of Cusco, Lima, and Tarapoto. Hip-hop artists Brenda Jah (Brenda Mejía) and Pedro Mo (Pedro Mosquera) were arrested in Lima and Cusco respectively and will reportedly be held for 15 days in preliminary detention, as requested by the Prosecutor’s Office specializing in terrorism offenses. In addition to the artists, leftist organizers Libia Arcila, David Tapullima, and Polidoro Tapullima were arrested and face a similar 15 days in preliminary detention. articles.title: Xi, Putin, and Trump meeting concludes with vague commitments, but strong symbolism
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Chinese President Xi Jinping held the first ever trilateral summit of Russia, China, and the US on the sidelines of the ongoing Asia-Pacific Economic Council (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19. The meeting, attended by Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, ended with a joint Declaration towards Peace with all three countries agreeing to find ways to work together on common issues including the need for reforms in the UN, global energy security, and rising nuclear risk. The declaration also talked about the principles of the operation of the International Criminal Court (ICC) and underlined the immunity for top state officials. articles.title: The daily reality of Israel’s mass extermination of life in Gaza
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: As Israel’s military aggression on the Gaza Strip enters its fourth year, devastating details continue to emerge regarding how every facet of daily life in Gaza has been engineered to maximize Palestinian casualties. In addition to fatalities caused directly by Israeli airstrikes, drones, artillery, and gunfire, the deprivation of basic necessities has been utilized as a weapon of war. This includes a lack of shelter during severe weather and acute shortages of food and essential supplies due to ongoing aid restrictions. articles.title: Anti-austerity protests continue with force in France
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Half a million people took part in demonstrations across France on Tuesday, November 17, in response to a strike call by public sector workers. Tuesday’s strike and protests marked the continuation of a mobilization wave that has shaken the country for approximately two months. “Today was the eleventh round of demonstrations since September 29,” wrote the General Confederation of Labor (CGT). “All in all, in two months, over 5 million demonstrators joined the mobilization for our public services and against the cost of living crisis.” Watch: France’s protest movement is fighting more than Macron “Workers continue to demonstrate their rejection of austerity policies, the deterioration of public services and the erosion of purchasing power,” echoed the trade union organization Solidaires . “

articles.title: Why I joined Tempest
articles.author: Keegan O'Brien
articles.content_excerpt: I’ m writing this message from Belfast, Northern Ireland. I’m on a solo trip around the country, and it’s been absolutely stunning. If you haven’t been to Ireland, I highly recommend making the trip! Today, I visited the James Connolly Museum, and the experience moved me to share some photos and brief reflections about my political life. These past seven-plus years since the dissolution of the International Socialist Organization have been a politically challenging time for me as a revolutionary socialist, as I know they have been for many others. At times, I still feel like I’ve lost my political home and anchor, struggling to stay afloat, make sense of what’s happening in the world, and figure out what comes next. articles.title: Why are Mexican cartels fighting in Ukraine?
articles.author: Zoe Alexandra
articles.content_excerpt: The war in Ukraine has become a training ground for Latin America’s drug cartels: An enforcer for one of Brazil’s biggest gangs was arrested in Rio this month after five on the front lines in Europe. Peter Korotaev, independent journalist and author of Events in Ukraine, joins Zoe Alexandra to unpack why Colombian ex-soldiers, Mexican cartel members and members of a Pentecostal Brazilian gang wound up among the foreign mercenaries fighting Russian forces. Some serve in units tied to HUR, Ukraine’s CIA-trained military intelligence agency, and to the far-right Azov movement, whose longtime leader Serhiy Korotkikh openly follows narco folk saint Santa Muerte.
